lead: Cape Coral plumbing deals with canals, hurricanes, a high water table and block homes from the 1960s on. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Cape Coral.
risk: storm-surge damage, slab leaks and well and septic conversions
risk_short: storm surge, slab leaks and septic
why: Southeast Cape Coral has homes from the 1960s and 1970s with cast-iron drains under the slab. Much of the north and west was built later, and some areas still use private wells and septic systems while the city expands utilities.
Hurricane Ian in 2022 pushed surge into thousands of canal-front homes. Flooded homes can have hidden damage in drains, water heaters and well pumps.
water: Cape Coral treats water from the Floridan Aquifer using reverse osmosis. It is soft after treatment. Homes outside the system use private wells.
tips: Shut off the main valve before a hurricane evacuation.
Have the water heater checked after any flood.
Know whether your home is on city water or a well.
Have cast-iron drains scoped in older homes.
areas: PipeMend works in the Yacht Club area, Cape Harbour, Pelican, Northwest Cape, Southeast Cape, Tarpon Point and every other Cape Coral neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Cape Coral Building Division, and plumbing contractors are licensed by the Florida Construction Industry Licensing Board.

faq.q: Is my Cape Coral home on city water?
faq.a: Many homes are, but some areas still use private wells and septic systems while the city extends utilities. Your utility bill, or the lack of one, tells you.
